package_info.why_malicious: This package is a typosquatted clone of a legitimate npm package, differing by a single character in the name. It delivers the r77 rootkit, a known malicious payload, to infected systems by executing a postinstall script that downloads and runs the rootkit, enabling stealthy persistence, privilege escalation, and unauthorized remote access.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code executes install.js, which initiates the download and execution of a remote rootkit binary, resulting in the installation of the r77 rootkit and enabling persistent attacker access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a postinstall script to execute additional code is a common malware technique, especially when the script is not required for legitimate package functionality and is used to download and run external binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages may use postinstall scripts for setup or compilation, but should never download and execute rootkits or make unauthorized system modifications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall scripts to compile native modules or set up dependencies, but they do not fetch and execute remote binaries or install rootkits.
key_indicators: Typosquatted package name closely resembling a popular library
Presence of a postinstall script in package.json that executes an external JavaScript file
Postinstall script initiates download and execution of a remote binary

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, install.js downloads a Windows executable (r77.exe) from a hardcoded remote server, writes it to C:\Windows\Temp, and executes it, resulting in the installation of the r77 rootkit and establishing persistent, stealthy attacker access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads an executable from an untrusted external domain and immediately executes it, a hallmark of malware delivery and rootkit installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download or execute remote binaries, especially not to system directories or without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some developer tools may self-update or fetch dependencies, but they do not download and execute arbitrary binaries from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Hardcoded external URL for binary download (https://malicious-domain.com/r77.exe)
Writes executable to a system directory (C:\Windows\Temp\r77.exe)
Executes the downloaded binary using child_process.exec
No user interaction or consent required for execution

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (node-hide-console-windows), mistaking it for a legitimate package due to typosquatting.
The postinstall script defined in package.json executes install.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in install.js is executed

attack_chain.action: install.js downloads the r77 rootkit from a remote server and executes it, installing the rootkit on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Rootkit is installed, attacker gains persistent and stealthy access

behavioral_signatures: npm package with a postinstall script that downloads and executes external binaries
Typosquatted package names that closely mimic popular libraries
Postinstall-time download and execution of Windows executables from hardcoded URLs
file_indicators: Presence of install.js containing network and process execution logic
Downloaded binary named r77.exe in C:\Windows\Temp
package.json with a postinstall script referencing install.js
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to untrusted or newly registered domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Download of r77.exe or similar payloads from external sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that download and execute binaries. Flag packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Detect outbound network requests to suspicious or untrusted domains during or immediately after package installation. Scan for the presence of known rootkit binaries (such as r77.exe) in temporary or system directories, and inspect install.js for network and process execution code.
